prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1465; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at an intersection, with the insured's vehicle struck on the driver side by a vehicle that entered from the cross street. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is represented by counsel, and all correspondence will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver with coverage in force at the time of loss. No coverage issues identified at this stage.

Entry 3: Police report, scene photographs and two independent witness statements all line up with the account given by the claimant and the other driver. The sequence of events appears consistent across every source collected so far.

Entry 4: Reviewed the damage estimate and photos. The vehicle damage is largely consistent with the described impact, with the heaviest deformation on the driver side. Still need to confirm exactly where the claimant was seated, since the accounts on this point are not fully clear.

Entry 5: A neighbor mentioned seeing the vehicle with damage several weeks before the reported loss date. Requested the neighbor's contact details and will follow up, though this is a single secondhand observation and nothing else in the file supports it yet. No earlier damage to the vehicle is recorded in our prior claims history.

Entry 6: Medical records show a shoulder injury with a treatment course that followed a typical pattern and eased off as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same area appears in the records obtained. The injury description fits the type and force of this collision.

Entry 7: The claimant has given the same account in each conversation, including the recorded statement and subsequent calls with counsel present. Based on the current file, the claim appears to be progressing normally, and I will keep the neighbor follow-up open pending their statement.
